blocks.content: The State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India.

rows: Positive Concept (equality of treatment under equal circumstances)
No man is above the law regardless of rank or condition
Like should be treated alike without any discrimination

items: Article 14 applies to both citizens and foreigners, whereas Articles 15, 16, and 19 apply exclusively to Indian citizens.
The word 'Untouchability' is neither defined in the Constitution of India nor in the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955.
National awards like Bharat Ratna and Padma Awards are not 'titles' under Article 18, as ruled by the Supreme Court in Balaji Raghavan case (1996).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws to all persons within the territory of India.
Article 15 prohibits discrimination against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex, or place of birth.
Article 16 ensures equality of opportunity for all citizens in matters relating to employment or appointment to any office under the State.
Article 17 abolishes 'Untouchability' and forbids its practice in any form, making it a punishable offense.
Article 18 abolishes titles and prohibits the State from conferring titles except military or academic distinctions.
